EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
  MINUTES
  SEPTEMBER 24, 2018

CALL TO ORDER
CHAIRMAN MITCHELL called the meeting to order, the time being 7:00 p.m. in the Rolling
Hills Estates City Council Chambers.

COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT
Chairman Judy Mitchell
Susan Brtis
Carol Dean-Porter
Patricia Harik
Carrie Silvano
Tim Zigrang
Vicki Shinn

STAFF MEMBER PRESENT
Andy Clark, Community Services Director

DRAFT MINUTES OF AUGUST 27, 2018
MEMBER BRTIS moved, seconded by MEMBER SILVANO

  TO APPROVE THE DRAFT MINUTES OF THE AUGUST 27, 2018 EQUESTRIAN
  COMMITTEE MEETING AS PRESENTED

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL SO ORDERED.

AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA
None

CALIFORNIA WATER SERVICE COMPANY WATER RELIABILITY PROJECT MONTHLY
UPDATE
Susan Cordone from California Water Service Company distributed project update fact sheets
and highlighted the progress made thus far. She reported that they were a few days behind
completing the installation of new pipes in the intersection of Palos Verdes Drive North and
Palos Verdes Drive East due to the discovery of unmarked water lines and a large amount of
sandy material buried in this intersection. They anticipate completing this intersection by
October 4, 2018.
EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
SEPTEMBER 24, 2018  1
 Ms. Cordone stated that she had inspected the Palomino Ranchos Trail that morning and
assured the Committee that every effort to save as many California Pepper trees along this
trail was being taken as they prepare to install pipes. She noted that the City will receive a
24-inch box tree for every tree removed and allowed to select the new planting site for each
replacement tree. The Community Services Director thanked California Water Service
Company for maintaining this trail for safe use during the September 15, 2018 City
Celebration event.

MEMBER SHINN reported that the loop trail detour on the Palos Verdes Landfill was uneven
and rocky in one section. The Community Services Director stated that he would contact the
Palos Verdes Landfill staff to re-grade this trail detour section.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL THANKED MS. CORDONE AND
RECEIVED AND FILED THIS AGENDA ITEM.

EQUINE EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS SUBCOMMITTEE MEETING UPDATE
MEMBER SHINN reported that a horse chipping clinic and trailering workshop would be held
at Ernie Howlett Park on Sunday, December 9, 2018 by the LA County Animal Care & Control
Department. The Community Services Director noted that this will be open to all LA County
residents, which eliminated the Peter Weber Equestrian Center facility from consideration.

Audience Member, Sean Martin, 2 Empty Saddle Road, stated that the Trailering Clinic date,
time, and location had not yet been finalized, but was still likely to be held this Fall.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL RECEIVED AND FILED THIS
AGENDA ITEM.

2018 CITY CELEBRATION EQUESTRIAN EVENTS DEBRIEFING
Audience Member Sean Martin, who coordinated the PVP Horsemens Association Poker
Ride event, reported that there was an increase in participation this year. The Community
Services Director noted that the City had received a check for $900 from PVPHA, which was
the most the City had received in many years. Mr. Martin indicated that the Horsemanship
Games went well and that he observed a large crowd of spectators staying later for the Battle
for the Saddle event. Finally, he noted that a brief electrical outage was quickly repaired
during the morning of the event, that an additional speaker(s) would be set up next year by
the sound service vendor, and that recruitment of equestrian and Poker Ride volunteers
needs to start earlier in 2019. MEMBER SHINN recommended watering the arena next year.

MEMBER SILVANO was thanked for her purchase of twelve stick horses for the new Stick
Horse Rodeo event and MEMBER SHINN was thanked for finding and paying Face Painters
for the event. CHAIRMAN MITCHELL encouraged both MEMBERS to submit receipts for
reimbursement. MEMBER SHINN suggested that two Corn Kernel Pits be installed next year,
possibly eliminate the Hay Jumping Pit, and to order three Birthday Cakes next year. She also
thanked Mr. Martin for his donation of the small toys that were awarded to the winners of the
Stick Horse Rodeo events in lieu of ribbons.
EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
SEPTEMBER 24, 2018  2
 CHAIRMAN MITCHELL suggested that we consider having the Palos Verdes Symphonic
Band perform next year. The Community Services Director stated that he would contact
Susan Seamans to find out what the fee or donation amount would be. MEMBER SHINN
recommended that we have a Country Western Band again next year and a Barbecue Dinner,
since it appears that equestrians and community members may stay later for this event.

CHAIRMAN MITCHELL thanked the Committee for their valuable input which will be shared
with City Council and the Park and Activities Commission during the upcoming City
Celebration Debriefing Meeting.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL RECEIVED AND FILED THIS
AGENDA ITEM.

EQUESTRIAN ISSUES LOG

MEMBER SHINN inquired whether the City could do anything about the mistreatment of the
horses at 84 Buckskin Lane. The Community Services Director responded that the City’s
Code Compliance staff member, an LA County Animal Care and Control Officer, and an
ASPCA Investigator had inspected the boarding facilities numerous times. During each visit a
bale of hay on-site to feed the horses and therefore enforcement action could not be initiated.
HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL RECEIVED AND FILED THE REPORT.

COMMITTEE MEMBER REPORTS
A.  ADOPT-A-TRAIL REPORTS

MEMBER SHINN reported that there was a piece of rebar sticking up on the trail located on
the west side of Hawthorne Boulevard. The Community Services Director indicated that it
would be removed immediately the next morning.

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS
A.  PV PENINSULA WATER RELIABILITY PROJECT UPDATE – Monthly

B.  EQUINE EMERGENCY RESPONSE PLAN UPDATE – Monthly

ADJOURNMENT
MEMBER SHINN moved, seconded by MEMBER SILVANO

  TO ADJOURN THE EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL ADJOURNED THE MEETING.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
SPETEMBER 24, 2018  3
 The meeting adjourned at 7:48 p.m.

Respectfully submitted,

Andy Clark
Community Services Director
